claims.claim: Stan!, who worked with Mohan for about ten years, says Mohan's job under whatever title was to set the editorial tone and mentor the staff.
claims.source: Stan! (Steven Brown), 50 Years in the Dungeon, 2025
claims.quote: always to set the editorial tone and mentor the staff

claims.claim: Stan! states that Mohan edited every edition of D&D from the original hardcovers to fifth-edition supplements.
claims.source: Stan! (Steven Brown), 50 Years in the Dungeon, 2025
claims.quote: worked on EVERY edition of D&D from the original hardcovers

claims.claim: Winninger's Second Rule of Dungeoncraft is that every major piece of the campaign world filled in must be given at least one secret related to it.
claims.quote: Whenever you fill in a major piece of the

claims.claim: The DUNGEON staff list failure to present information in the proper D&D style among the standard reasons an article is rejected.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Rejection
claims.quote: failure to present information in the proper D&D style

claims.claim: A DUNGEON Backdrop, the magazine's locale feature, may range in scope from a demiplane down to a single city location such as a tavern or temple.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Features
claims.quote: from a demiplane to a single city location

claims.claim: The DUNGEON guidelines require surprises and plot twists to be outlined in the synopsis for the DM rather than sprung during the adventure text.
claims.source: The DUNGEON Staff, DUNGEON Submission Guidelines, Adventure Synopsis

claims.claim: Wizards of the Coast describes the SRD as containing the base game rules, naming the rules glossary, weapon mastery properties and exploration mechanics as its content.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / DND Staff, "You Can Now Publish Your Own Creations Using the New Core Rules", D&D Beyond
claims.quote: such as the rules glossary, weapon mastery properties, and exploration mechanics

claims.claim: Shawn Merwin tells adventure writers to avoid using D&D’s mechanical terms in their ordinary senses inside boxed text.
claims.source: Shawn Merwin, "Let’s Design an Adventure: Boxed Text", D&D Beyond
claims.quote: Avoid game mechanical terms used in a non-mechanical way

claims.claim: A reader on the official D&D Beyond forum states that the planes-of-existence section has been removed from SRD 5.2 while the plane names survive inside the rules.
claims.source: Forum user SteelfistBrave1, "Official SRD 5.2 Discussion Thread", D&D Beyond forums
claims.quote: the section about the planes of existence has been removed

claims.claim: The independent Creative Commons rendering of SRD 5.1 at 5thsrd.org carries the planes-appendix sentences word for word as extracted from the PDF, confirming the extraction the figures rest on.
claims.source: 5thSRD, "The Planes of Existence" (community CC-BY rendering of SRD 5.1)
claims.quote: It is a great, silvery sea, the same above and below
